About Security Report

About WebPerformance Report

WebPerformance Report is a reporting service. It gathers data from the tools you already trust and turns it into a clear report delivered to your inbox, on your schedule. Free to start, no dashboard to keep checking.

The HTTP Observatory Report shows how your site’s HTTP security headers are graded: Content Security Policy, HSTS, cookies, CORS, redirections, Referrer Policy, SRI and X-Frame-Options, plus the raw server headers and what changed since the last report.

See the security report

Where the data comes from

The HTTP Observatory is developed by Mozilla and runs on MDN. It analyzes the response headers your server returns and checks them against security best practices widely accepted across the web industry.

Those headers defend your site against clickjacking, code injection and man-in-the-middle attacks, and they are easy to overlook.

Inside the Web Security Report

Weak security headers leave your visitors more exposed: injected scripts can steal what they type, hidden frames can trick them into clicks, and downgraded connections can be intercepted, often unnoticed because nothing looks broken. Every report shows where your headers stand across the four areas below, and what to prioritize.

  • Scan summary

    Your site’s grade and score from Mozilla’s HTTP Observatory, with how many tests pass and how many fail.

  • Scoring

    The penalty behind each result, CSP, CORS, redirections, Referrer Policy, HSTS, SRI, X-Content-Type and X-Frame-Options, so you can prioritize the biggest ones.

  • CSP analysis

    Whether your Content Security Policy blocks inline scripts, eval(), plug-ins and insecure content: the protections against code injection.

  • Raw server headers

    The headers your server actually sends, including ones like Server and X-Powered-By that can reveal your technology stack.
